newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pernod unit sees Two Dogs tied up in January.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pernod unit sees Two Dogs tied up in January.

text.p: Australian wine producer Orlando Wyndham, a subsidiary of Pernod-Ricard of France, said on Tuesday it expects to finalise its proposed 100 percent acquisition of Two Dogs Holdings Ltd by the end of January 1997.

Orlando managing director Jean-Louis Lepeltier told Reuters the acquisition of the unlisted producer of "Two Dogs" alcoholic lemonade, announced earlier, was subject to Two Dogs shareholder approval and Australian foreign investment rules.
"If you put these things together, the sale will be effective towards the end of January," he said.
Shareholders of Two Dogs Holdings Ltd will meet on December 13, he said. Lepeltier said he could not reveal the price Orlando would pay, due to commercial confidentiality agreements.
"Two Dogs" creator and founder Duncan MacGillivray, the majority shareholder, would remain as managing director of the holding company, he said.
Lepeltier likened the potential of "Two Dogs", which was launched two years ago and now sells in 44 countries, to Orlando's Jacob's Creek, one of Australia's top selling wine export brands.

He said Pernod Ricard had the financial resources and distribution network to strengthen Two Dogs worldwide potential, and the acquisition would give it the opportunity to expand its own designer drinks portfolio.
"From both sides, I think it is a good arrangement," he said.
"Two Dogs" is currently brewed in Australia, the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States.
Lepeltier said the group had not yet reviewed production facilities but would look at the most economic situation, subject to negotiation with contractors.
Two Dogs has said it expects to sell five million cases of its alcoholic lemonade this year.
